title: Crypto Account Safety: Why 2FA Matters More Than a Strong Password
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Two-factor authentication adds a second lock to your accounts, and authenticator apps are generally safer than text messages. Sources: CISA, Coinbase Learn. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: ONE PASSWORD IS NOT ENOUGH
scenes.narration: Your crypto account has a strong password. But what if that password leaks? One lock is not enough.

scenes.head: WHAT IS 2FA?
scenes.narration: Two factor authentication, or two F A, asks for a second proof. Something you know, plus something you have.

scenes.head: WHY IT MATTERS
scenes.narration: Passwords can be stolen by fake sites or leaked in data breaches. A second step can stop a thief who has your password.

scenes.head: TEXT MESSAGE 2FA
scenes.sub: PHONE NUMBERS CAN BE TAKEN OVER
scenes.narration: Codes sent by text can be risky. Criminals sometimes trick phone companies into moving your number to their phone.

scenes.head: A SAFER CHOICE
scenes.narration: Security agencies suggest authenticator apps or hardware keys, which are generally safer than text message codes.

scenes.head: GOOD HABITS
scenes.narration: Use a unique password for each site, keep backup codes offline, and never share a code with anyone, even support.

scenes.head: ONE CRYPTO BASIC A DAY
